$comment: SHIPPED OrgProfile schema — the DATA half of `brain.org_setup`, kept out of the code for the same reason naming-contract.json is: the wizard, the validator and the docs must not be able to disagree about what a profile is. Two schemas live here. `answers` describes the SIX things a leader must supply because no scan can discover them; `profile` describes the artifact the wizard emits (the Phase-7 OrgProfile that `brain-init --profile` consumes). Nothing here names an organisation: every example is a placeholder, and the real org arrives at runtime from the leader's answers.

validator.$comment: The supported keyword subset, deliberately small — this is a hand-rolled stdlib validator (task-station ships no third-party dependency), so an unsupported keyword must be a loud authoring error rather than a silently skipped check.

answers.$comment: THE SIX UNDISCOVERABLE ANSWERS. A scan reads what an org already wrote down; these are decisions nobody has written down anywhere a scan can reach, so the wizard must ask. `forge_project` is the seventh field only because ADO needs a project segment where GitHub does not — it is part of answer 4, not a new answer.

org_slug.description: answer 1 — the org's short identity, kebab-case, used to name everything downstream

org_brain_repo.description: answer 2 — the repo name of the shared ORG brain on the forge

mirror_template.description: answer 3 — the per-person mirror NAMING TEMPLATE. Binding ruling 2026-08-15: a template resolved from the host identity at init, never a literal an admin types, which is why the placeholder is required rather than optional

forge_kind.description: answer 4a — which git forge adapter (core.forge) drives promotion

forge_url.description: answer 4b — the forge's org URL, e.g. https://example.com/your-org

forge_project.description: answer 4c — the ADO project segment; required for forge_kind=ado, absent for github

forge_target_branch.description: optional — the org brain's integration branch (default main)

vertical_pack.description: answer 5 — which opt-in vocabulary pack from naming-contract.json applies, or null for none. Checked against the shipped pack list, not against a copy of it here

promotion_approvers.description: answer 6 — who may approve an org-brain promotion PR. An empty list would mean promotion is ungated, so the floor is one

org_label.description: optional — display name for the shared org wiki; derived from org_slug when absent

labels.description: optional — the two tier labels; brain.config falls back to built-in generics when absent

profile.$comment: THE EMITTED ARTIFACT. Keys `org_label`, `labels`, `keywords` and `forge` are the Phase-7 shape `brain.init_home._apply_profile` reads — their names are fixed by that consumer, not chosen here. Everything else is the wizard's own record: the leader's decisions that are not forge settings, the scanned vocabulary, and the provenance that says which scan produced what.

domains.description: the org's domain words mapped to a generic area — the payload of the org brain's schemas/node-types.json

unmapped_domains.description: discovered words with no area a shipped hint can justify. Listed rather than guessed: a wrong area is a filter that silently stops matching, and the org half of the registry is PR-gated on purpose
